claims.statement: The entire-thread breakdown formatter refuses to render unless it receives a version-one breakdown whose `historical_complete` flag is true, so incomplete legacy detail cannot be presented as a complete token table.

For a valid breakdown, the plain-text table marks incomplete categories as partial or unavailable, identifies directionless cost not attributable to input or output, and warns when some requests were unpriceable.

`CostBreakdownScreen` is a read-only live modal: it rejects duplicate stacking, refreshes its provider every half second while retaining the previous view on provider failure, and uses sanitized non-markup text for display and clipboard copy.

`CostTrackingMiddleware` owns additive private checkpoint channels for cumulative dollars and structured cost detail, drains completed records after model work and agent completion, and keeps tracking failures from failing a user turn by restoring records where possible.

Pricing is best effort: unsupported models and malformed usage return no estimate rather than interrupting the model turn, while the version-one breakdown records total versus priced request counts and completeness for categories.

`PreparedOperationCost` destructively claims recorder entries and must be committed with its additive checkpoint update or rolled back; restoring after a landed write can double charge, whereas abandoning a prepared value permanently loses its claimed spend.

Prompt-cache policy is intentionally available only for official provider endpoints or exact user-trusted hosts, and routes that cross provider wire formats resolve to no policy rather than asserting a cache-retention guarantee.

Thread checkpoint writes are fenced by an operating-system-backed per-thread lease and token: the owned SQLite saver validates the reservation and token inside a serialized writer guard, rejecting stale writers after release or ownership change.

Thread deletion acquires the ownership reservation, rejects a live thread owned elsewhere, removes checkpoint/write rows and side-question cost, then best-effort deletes offloaded history; its return value reports checkpoint deletion rather than archive cleanup.

The server-side offload route serializes work per thread, requires a registered idle thread without pending graph work, validates that the checkpoint did not advance before commit, and allowlists its state update so it cannot write conversation messages.

Offload settles prepared model cost with the checkpoint update: it rolls back only when a failed write is confirmed unchanged, keeps records claimed for advanced or unreadable writes to avoid double charging, and completes commit work before re-raising cancellation.

Normal server offload commits summary state and cost before deferred archive append and link, while a handoff preserves source context and commits only source cost channels plus a source-owned recovery transcript.

`SessionStats` records estimates and tokens by provider/model and usage kind, and its streamed-request ledger retracts and replaces earlier chunk contributions so one API request is counted once even when usage arrives incrementally or its model attribution is refined.

The client only accepts a nested model-usage event after validating its event version, required identifiers and usage fields, and active thread; invalid, unsupported, or stale-thread events do not alter provisional usage statistics.

Thread listing creates a covering metadata index before grouping checkpoints, populates names separately, and defers expensive checkpoint-derived message count and initial-prompt enrichment; the derived-field caches are keyed by the latest checkpoint identity so changed checkpoints are reloaded.

Thread names are constrained to trimmed printable single-line values of 1–50 characters and are saved transactionally in `dcode_thread_names` while mirroring the latest checkpoint for compatibility; reads prefer the durable table and fall back to latest checkpoint metadata.

The `/threads` selector can paint cached rows before database refresh and fetches message counts or initial prompts only when their columns are visible and missing; application startup and post-turn refresh prewarm this cache in a background worker.

`/threads -r` resumes the previously reset thread or the most recent active-agent thread when no ID is supplied, while an explicit target may require an agent switch; a normal thread switch reserves the destination first and releases ownership only after its outcome is known.

The built-in thread inspector is a read-only tool for trusted local sessions: it uses strict MsgPack deserialization to inspect the latest checkpoint and falls back to replaying writes, while its documented default database resolution follows `DEEPAGENTS_HOME` and `DEEPAGENTS_SESSIONS_DB`.

Side-question and thread-name model spend is persisted as a separate sessions-database subtotal rather than returned to graph checkpoint cost channels; a deletion tombstone prevents late completion or retry from recreating deleted spend.

The once-per-process pricing updater preserves the current catalog when an upstream snapshot has fewer providers than the bundled catalog, while offline mode or a disabled `update.prices_auto_update` option prevents updater startup.

When primary pricing lacks a model, dcode can load user and bundled provider-schema override catalogs; user entries take precedence for colliding provider/model pairs, deterministic loading is cached for the process, and primary upstream coverage supersedes an override.

The thread inspector opens only a read-only database with required checkpoint and write tables, resolves only root-namespace thread records, and reconstructs messages from strict MsgPack checkpoint data with ordered-write replay as its fallback.
